name: Long hair is law

card.summary: A looksmaxxing saying holding that growing out hair is the single biggest styling change a man can make to look better.

quick.overview:
"Long hair is law" is forum shorthand for the belief that hair length and volume change a man's overall look more than most other styling choices. Proponents say longer hair frames the face, softens or balances the jaw and forehead, and adds visual mass, so growing it out is presented as a high-impact, low-cost step.

The phrase is community slang rather than a studied concept. No published trial has tested it directly, though research on hair and attractiveness, and on how hairstyle changes perception of face shape, exists in broader form.
quick.how: In practice people grow their hair for several months, then ask a barber for a shape suited to their face and hair type, often using a cut that keeps length at the top and sides. Hair grows roughly 0.6 to 3.4 cm per month according to Wikipedia, so growing out takes time.
quick.risks: There are no health risks to growing hair out. Thinning or receding hair may change how a longer style looks, and some workplaces and schools set grooming rules. Reception of long hair on men varies by culture and setting.

lead: "Long hair is law" is a looksmaxxing slogan asserting that longer hair is the strongest style lever available to men. It appears in forum threads on looksmax.org as a declarative one-liner, often paired with photos of men with and without long hair [1].

Believers argue that length adds frame around the face, hides or offsets features they dislike, and signals health and confidence. Scalp hair grows roughly 0.6 to 3.4 cm per month, so the approach is gradual [2].

The claim has not been tested as stated. Hair has long carried social meaning, from subcultural identity (hippies, metalheads) to religious practice, and attitudes to men's hair length have shifted by era and place [2].

chain: Hair frames the face and changes perceived face shape
Overall look changes with no procedure
angle.text: Proponents see growing hair as a free change that reshapes how the face is framed. The result depends on hair density, texture and face shape.

paras: Supporters hold that hair length matters more than most grooming choices, since hair surrounds the face and affects perceived proportions. Threads on looksmax.org share before-and-after photos to illustrate this [1].

Long hair on men has been tied to counterculture, to religious rules such as the Sikh obligation not to cut hair, and to historic political divides such as the English Civil War, according to Wikipedia's article on hair [2].

lore.intro: The phrase circulates as a short slogan in looksmax.org threads [1].

claims.claim: Long hair is the strongest style lever
claims.believers: Posters present length as the single largest visual change available without surgery [1].
claims.experts: No published studies have tested this ranking against other styling choices.
